failures.title: Porsche MA2.76 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Water Pump Wear
items.whatHappens: Like many modern Porsche engines, the MA2.76's water pump can develop leaks or seize due to plastic impeller degradation. Symptoms include coolant loss, overheating, and unusual noises from the pump area.
items.repairVsReplace: Water pump replacement is a routine but moderately labour‑intensive repair (£800-£1,500 at a specialist). If overheating occurs, cylinder head inspection may be needed. Read our full water pump failure guide

items.title: Oil Leaks from Camshaft Covers
items.whatHappens: The MA2.76 can develop oil leaks from the camshaft cover gaskets and timing chain covers. These are not catastrophic but can lead to low oil levels and potential bearing damage if ignored.
items.repairVsReplace: Gasket replacement is labour‑intensive but straightforward (8-12 hours). If oil starvation has occurred, bearing damage may require a full rebuild.

items.title: High‑Pressure Fuel Pump Issues (if applicable)
items.whatHappens: Some variants of the MA2.76 may experience high‑pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failures, causing rough running, misfires, and check engine lights.
items.repairVsReplace: HPFP replacement typically costs £800-£1,500 at a specialist. Not catastrophic but can be inconvenient.

failures.goodYearsLine: The MA2.76 benefits from Porsche's ongoing development, with no major catastrophic failures reported. It is considered more reliable than earlier M96/M97 engines, with fewer concerns over IMS bearings or bore scoring. Regular servicing and preventative water pump replacement are key to longevity.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the MA2.76
variants.intro: The MA2.76 is the 2.9‑litre naturally aspirated variant of Porsche's MA series, fitted to entry‑level 718 Boxster and Cayman models. It is distinguished from the larger 3.0L, 3.4L, 3.8L and 4.0L flat‑sixes by displacement and power output. Where the code appears: - On the engine block - stamped on the left‑hand side near the oil filter housing - On the V5C registration document (engine number field) - Via Porsche VIN decoder - the 8th character of the VIN indicates engine type Commonly confused codes: - MA2.75 - 2.0L turbocharged flat‑four (718 base) - MA2.77 - 2.5L turbocharged flat‑four (718 S) - 9A2.10 - 4.0L naturally aspirated flat‑six (718 GTS 4.0/GT4) - MA1.20 - earlier 2.9L flat‑six (987.2) Why fitting the wrong revision matters: The MA2.76 is not interchangeable with turbocharged flat‑fours or the 4.0L flat‑six. ECU calibration, engine mounts, exhaust manifolds, and cooling systems all differ. Fitting a different engine would require extensive modifications.

relatives.description: the earlier 2.9L naturally aspirated flat-six that powered the 987.2-generation Boxster and Cayman. The MA2.76 replaced it in the 718 generation with improved emissions and minor refinement, though the basic character remains similar.

the higher-output turbocharged flat-four fitted to the 718 S and GTS. It shares the same basic architecture but uses forced induction for significantly more power.
the larger, more powerful 4.0L flat-six fitted to the top-tier 718 models. If you're considering an upgrade, note that the 4.0L unit is not a direct fit and requires extensive modifications.

options.body: ** A used MA2.76 can make sense for a 718 owner on a budget, but only if the engine comes with full service history and documented water pump / cam cover gasket replacements. Without this, the risk of hidden cooling or oil leak issues is significant.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper MA2.76 recon addresses the engine's specific failure points: water pump replacement, cam cover gaskets, oil system service, and full gasket and seal replacement. This is the right call for a well‑maintained 718 where the car's value justifies the spend - a £35,000-£55,000 718 Boxster/Cayman comfortably absorbs a £12,500-£16,000 reconditioned engine.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified for the MA2.76 when the original block is still sound but has suffered water pump or oil leak damage. For lower‑value examples, a rebuild may be more cost‑effective than a full reconditioned unit.

items.question: How much does a Porsche MA2.76 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned MA2.76 2.9L engine costs from £12,500-£16,000 supply-only . Used units range £4,500-£8,000, while a full rebuild can cost £8,000-£12,000 depending on the extent of damage. Supply-only prices exclude fitting; independent Porsche specialists charge £80-£100/hr for 12-16 hours of labour. Prices vary by condition and mileage - units with documented water pump and cam cover gasket replacement carry a premium. The MA2.76 is one of the more affordable Porsche flat-six engines to replace. Water pump and gasket condition are the key factors affecting replacement viability.

items.question: What are the common problems with the MA2.76 engine?
items.answer: The most significant known issues are water pump wear (40k-70k miles) and oil leaks from camshaft covers and timing chain covers (40k-80k miles). Some variants may experience high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) issues at similar mileages. The MA2.76 benefits from Porsche's ongoing development and has no major catastrophic failures reported - it is considered a robust and reliable entry-level flat-six. Water pump failure can cause overheating - address preventatively at 60,000 miles. Oil leaks are not catastrophic if caught early, but can lead to bearing failure if ignored. No IMS bearing or bore scoring concerns on the MA2.76.

items.question: Which Porsche models use the MA2.76 engine?
items.answer: The MA2.76 2.9L naturally aspirated flat-six is fitted to the 718-generation Boxster and Cayman base models and T variants (2016-present). It serves as the entry-level naturally aspirated engine in the 718 range. The engine is not used in any other model; it is Porsche-specific. The MA2.76 is the base engine - always confirm you have a 718 Boxster or Cayman. The 718 S and GTS use turbocharged flat-fours (MA2.77 and MA2.75). The 718 GTS 4.0 and GT4 use the larger 4.0L 9A2.10 flat-six.

items.question: Should I buy a used, reconditioned, or rebuilt MA2.76?
items.answer: A used MA2.76 can be viable if it has full service history and documented water pump/cam cover gasket replacement - the absence of catastrophic IMS or bore scoring concerns makes used units less risky than earlier M96/M97 engines. Reconditioned is the safest option, as a proper recon includes a new water pump, cam cover gaskets, oil system service, and full seal replacement. A full rebuild is justified if your original block is still sound but has suffered water pump or oil leak damage - though rebuilds are less common on the MA2.76 than on earlier engines. For a high-value 718 Boxster S-spec, reconditioned is strongly recommended. For a higher-mileage example, a used engine with documented service history may be more cost-effective. Always insist on a warranty of at least 12 months for any replacement.

items.question: How do I confirm my car has the MA2.76 engine and not another variant?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on the engine block and appears on your V5C registration document. The most reliable way to confirm is via Porsche VIN decoder - the 8th character of the VIN indicates engine type. Critical: the MA2.76 is a 2.9L naturally aspirated flat-six - if your car is a 718 S or GTS, it has a turbocharged flat-four, not the MA2.76. The 8th character of the VIN identifies the engine type. The MA2.76 has 2,893 cc displacement and is fitted to 718 Boxster/Cayman base models. Do not confuse with the MA2.75 (2.0L turbo flat-four) or MA2.77 (2.5L turbo flat-four).

items.question: Is the MA2.76 a reliable engine?
items.answer: The MA2.76 is considered a robust and reliable entry-level flat-six. It benefits from Porsche's ongoing development and has no major catastrophic failures reported - unlike the M96/M97, there are no IMS bearing or bore scoring concerns. The primary weaknesses are the water pump and cam cover gaskets - both are repairable without engine replacement. With proper maintenance (regular oil changes, water pump replacement at 60k miles), an MA2.76 can comfortably exceed 100,000 miles. Regular oil changes (every 6,000-8,000 miles or annually) are critical. Water pump replacement is recommended at 60,000 miles as a preventative measure. Cam cover gasket inspection is recommended at 50,000 miles.
